attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated as his own assertion, not quoted from anyone else.

semantics.note: 'Still isn't making profit' is an unhedged present-tense observation. 'OpenAI is not profitable' captures it without adding or dropping anything.

contract.note: The plain reading (company-wide net income, H1 2025, the latest half-year before the post) is fair and ordinary. The contract also says an unknown accounting basis blocks any grade. That conflicts with the policy's plain-reading rule, so I don't apply it. A loss this large would not plausibly turn into a profit under a different basis.

evidence.note: Reuters, dated before the evaluation date, quotes a named portfolio manager saying OpenAI reported a $13.5B net loss in H1 2025. It is secondhand and not the underlying accounts, but it is credible reporting of reported results, which the contract allows, and it covers the right metric and period.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair plain reading (OpenAI had no positive net income in H1 2025), e1 reports a $13.5B net loss on $4.3B revenue for that half-year. No counterevidence in the packet shows a profit. The contract's internal clause that bars grading over the accounting basis is not part of the policy, and with a loss this size the basis does not change the sign. The source is secondhand, but it meets the contract's source requirements.
